page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. The instance features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 8.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), and AES cryptography.

Hardware bundling does not include integrated local instance storage, requiring persistent data to rely on external cloud storage volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with this profile.

Synthetic benchmarks place the ecs.c6e.xlarge mostly within lower tiers compared to the broader cloud server population. Stress-ng scores show 1312.8 in single-core and 3490.35 in multi-core metrics, both falling into the bottom 25%. Geekbench performance yields an average single-core score of 1160.0 alongside a multi-core score of 2539.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 25.0 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 21.81 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific operations measured 3.32 million operations per second in Redis SET throughput and 3.78 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency is oriented toward entry-level dedicated computing requirements where consistent compute availability is preferred over burstable pooling. Given the 1:2 RAM-to-CPU ratio, lack of built-in NVMe storage, and moderate networking capacity, the instance is appropriate for lightweight web serving, batch task execution, basic continuous integration pipelines, and small computational workloads.
